title: Canonical-byte polynomial arithmetic for cyclic_decomposition chain_polys
description:
Replace the scalar Montgomery polynomial-bookkeeping inside `cyclic_decomposition`'s `chain_polys` updates with canonical-byte polynomial arithmetic for `Fp

` with `P ≤ 251`, removing the ~16M Montgomery REDC operations that dominate `GF(251)/n=256` charpoly. ## Background `d1dd266c` landed `PackedFpMatrix

` + `PackedFpBasis

` so the matvec and basis-reduce arms of `cyclic_decomposition` run in canonical-byte form. The remaining hot path is the polynomial-bookkeeping loop that updates `chain_polys[k]` after each Krylov step — each update is `O(k)` field operations × `O(k)` substitutions, totalling `O(n^3)` Montgomery muls at `n=256`. Empirically: ~16M Mont muls × ~10 ns ≈ 160 ms estimated; measured 12.6 ms (zero-coefficient skips help). fflas runs the equivalent in 1.3 ms. ## Hard ceilings (fflas-ffpack reference) | Cell | fflas wall | 1.5x ceiling | Current gf2 wall | Current ratio | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | GF(251)/n=256 charpoly | 1.317 ms | 1.975 ms | 12.61 ms | 9.58x FAIL | ## Success Criteria - [hard] `GF(251)/n=256` charpoly meets the 1.5x ceiling (≤ 1.975 ms) on the current Zen 3 host. - [hard] `cyclic_decomposition`'s `chain_polys` updates execute in canonical-byte arithmetic for `Fp

` with `P ≤ 251`, with no Montgomery REDC inside the inner update loop. Scalar Montgomery path is retained as a fallback for non-`Fp` fields and for `P > 251`. - [hard] No regression on any other charpoly or minpoly cell currently PASSing. - [hard] Correctness: existing `cyclic_decomposition` invariants continue to pass; add a proptest comparing the canonical-byte chain_polys output to the scalar Montgomery output across random matrices over `Fp<7>` and `Fp<251>`, sizes n ∈ {2..32}. - [hard] Final evidence updates `dev/bench_results/2026-05-07-d1dd266c-minpoly-tuning.md` (or a successor doc) with the new GF(251)/n=256 charpoly Criterion median + before/after comparison. ## Notes The replacement should ideally also speed up `GF(7)/n=256` charpoly (currently 0.82x — already PASSing, but the same algorithmic path benefits). No regression target on that cell; just measure post-implementation. `d1dd266c` is blocked on this task.
